Yes. Although, the number of people who claim to be direct witnesses to the gas chambers is relatively small. Early witness statements are also at odds with later witness statements, and a critical reading of the testimonies show them to be generally inconsistent with each other, and with the physical evidence. Indeed, testimony of electrocution facilities and steam chambers were a feature of early testimonial evidence. The steam chambers even made it to Nuremberg, as did samples of human soap (now debunked), shrunken heads (see this documentary), and claims of gassings at Buchenwald and Dachau.

What I found very interesting is that it was initially claimed there were gassings at perhaps 10 other camps in Germany and Austria (aside from the six claimed today in Poland) which all had witnesses -- and even confessions from Nazis. Mainstream historians debunked these claims in the 60's. The six camps that were left were held by the Soviets, who wouldn't allow investigation by the west. (Lobbying and the cultural entrenchment of the myth eventually made debunking further gas chambers impractical.)
